title: Separate approximation from passage to a limit
obstacle: An infinite construction is easier to compare on finite or otherwise controlled approximants.
procedure: Prove the needed relation for the approximants.
Establish convergence in the topology required by the chosen operation.
Use an applicable continuity or limit theorem with its hypotheses proved, then identify the limit.
verification: Check the approximating relation, convergence hypotheses and exact limit theorem separately in Lean.
positive_example: Pass a proved relation through a continuous map after proving convergence.
negative_example: Commute an arbitrary operation with a limit from pointwise convergence alone.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.
